जीर: जीर जीर, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. जिन्व्), Ved. quick, speedy, lively, active, busy; driving, exciting; गो-जीर, exciting (the milk of) the cows; (अस्), m. quick motion or movement (especially of the Soma stones); a sword, a scymitar, a sacrificial knife; Panicum Miliaceum; cumin-seed, (in this latter sense said to be fr. rt. जु or 1. जॄ।) —जीर-दानु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. dropping, trickling, drizzling, sprinkling or scattering in small drops; causing to flow abundantly; (Sāy.) ‘granting a victorious dis-position’ (as if fr. rt. 1. जि). —जीराध्वर (°र-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having animated or vigorous rites; (Sāy.) free from injury or molestation. —जीराश्व (°र-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having lively or fleet horses.
जीरक: जीरक or जीरण, अस्, m. cumin-seed.
जीरि: जीरि, इस्, m. f., Ved. quick or flowing water.
जीरिका: जीरिका, f., N. of a plant, = जीर्ण-पत्त्रिका।
जीर्ण: जीर्ण जीर्ण। See under rt. 1. जॄ।

जीर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, old, ancient; worn out, wasted, withered, decayed, ruined, in ruins; digested; (अस्), m. an old man; a tree; cumin-seed; (आ), f. large cumin-seed; (अम्), n. decrepitude, old age; benja-min. —जीर्ण-ज्वर or जीर्णामय-ज्वर, अस्, m. a lingering fever with diminishing intensity. —जीर्ण-ज्वरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, affected with the above fever. —जीर्ण-टीका, f. ‘the ancient commentary,’ title of an astronomical work. —जीर्ण-ता, f. or जीर्ण-त्व, अम्, n. old age; infirmity, decay. —जीर्ण-दारु, उस्, m. the plant Convolvulus Argenteus. —जीर्ण-पत्त्रिका, f. ‘having withered leaves,’ N. of a plant, = वंश-पत्त्री. —जीर्ण-पर्ण, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘having withered leaves,’ the plant Nauclea Cadamba. —जीर्ण-फञ्जी, f. = जीर्ण-दारु. —जीर्ण-बुध्न, अस्, m. a kind of Lodhra. —जीर्ण-बुध्नक, अम्, n. a kind of Cyperus. —जीर्ण-वज्र, अम्, n. a gem, said to be a sort of diamond. —जीर्ण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, old decayed. —जीर्ण-वस्त्र, अम्, n. old, worn or tattered raiment; (अस्, आ, अम्), wearing old clothes. —जीर्ण-वाटिका, f. a ruined house. —जीर्ण-व्रध्-नक, अस्, m. a fragrant grass, Cyperus Rotundus. —जीर्णोद्धार (°ण-उद्°), अस्, m. the repairing of what is worn out, renewal, repairs. —जीर्णोद्धृत (°ण-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, rescued from decay, repaired. —जीर्णोद्यान (°ण-उद्°), अम्, n. a neglected garden.
जीर्वि: जीर्वि जीर्वि, इस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. जॄ), an axe; a cart; the body; an animal.
जीव्: जीव् जीव्, cl. 1. P. (poet. also A.) जीवति, -ते, जिजीव, जीविष्यति, जीवितुम्, to live, be alive; to revive, return to life; to make a liveli-hood, live by (with inst.): Caus. P. (ep. also A.) जीवयति, -ते, -यितुम्, to make alive, restore to life, vivify; to support life, to keep alive; to nourish, nurture, bring up; (a Causal form जीवापयति occasionally occurs, meaning ‘to restore to life’): Desid. जिजीविषति (Ved. जुज्यूषति or जिज्यूषति), to wish to live, to seek a livelihood, wish to live by (with inst.); [cf. Lith. gywénu, ‘to live;’ gywas, ‘alive:’ Slav. schivû, ‘to live:’ Goth. qvivs: Old Germ. qveh: Angl. Sax. cvic: Eng. quick: Lat. vivo.]
जीव: जीव, अस्, आ, अम्, living, existing, a living being; causing to live, vivifying; (अस्), m. the principle of life, the vital breath, the living or personal soul in-corporated in the body and imparting to it life, motion, and sensation, (hence also called जीवात्मन्; it is distinguished from the परमात्मन् or supreme soul, q. v.); livelihood, profession, specific occupa-tion; a kind of plant; an epithet of Bṛhaspati as regent of the planet Jupiter; or as regent of the Nakṣatra Tiṣya or Puṣya; the third lustrum in the cycle of Jupiter which lasts sixty years; N. of one of the eight Maruts; an epithet of Karṇa; (अस्, अम्), m. n. life, existence; (आ), f. the living or life-giving element, i. e. water; the earth; a bow-string; (in geometry) the chord of an arc, the sine of an arc; the tinkling of metallic ornaments; N. of two plants, = जीवन्ती and वचा; [cf. Lith. gywas, ‘alive;’ Goth. qvivs; Lat. vivus; Gr. βίος; Hib. beo, ‘living, alive.’] —जीव-गृभ्, -घृप्, प्, प्, Ved. taking alive, seizing beings alive. —जीव-ग्रह, अस्, m., Ved. filling (a cup) with the living Soma, i. e. with the plant in its unpressed state. —जीव-ग्राह, अस्, m. a prisoner, one taken alive; जीव-ग्राहं ग्रह्, to capture alive. —जीव-घोष-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a grammarian. —जीव-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born alive. —जीव-जीव or जीव-जीवक, अस्, m. a kind of bird; see the next. —जीवञ्-जीव, अस्, m. a kind of bird supposed to be a pheasant; the Chakor or Greek partridge; a kind of tree. —जीव-तोका, f. a woman whose children are living. —जीव-त्व, अम्, n. the state of life or existence. —१। जीव-द, अस्, आ, अम् (rt. दा), ‘life-giving,’ who or what gives life; (अस्), m. a physician, a practitioner of medicine. —२। जीव-द, अस्, m. (rt. दो), ‘cutting off life,’ an enemy. —जीव-दशा, f. mortal existence. —जीव-दात्री, f. ‘life-giver,’ a kind of medicinal plant, = ऋद्धि। —जीव-दान, अम्, n. ‘giving life,’ ‘rescuing from sickness,’ title of a manual of medicine composed by Cyavana. —जीव-दानु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. a wrong form for जीर-दानु, q. v. —जीव-दामन्, आ, m., N. of a prince. —जीव-दायक, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘life-giving.’ —जीव-धन, अम्, n. ‘living wealth,’ property in living creatures, live stock, wealth in flocks and herds. —जीव-धन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘supporting living beings;’ (Sāy.) ‘satiating living beings,’ an epithet of Soma, and of Prajā-pati. —जीव-धानी, f. ‘receptacle of living beings,’ an epithet of the earth. —जीव-नश्, क्, क्, क्, or ट्, ट्, ट्, (a sacrifice &c.) where living beings are killed. —जीव-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of a writer on astronomy; N. of a physician. —जीव-नाय or जीव-नायक, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —जीव-नाशम्, ind. with नश्, to lose one's life, die, perish. —जीव-निकाय, अस्, m. a being endowed with life. —जीव-नेत्री, f., N. of a plant, = सैंहली. —जीव-पति, इस्, m. a living husband. —जीव-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a fresh leaf. —जीवपत्त्र-प्रचायिका, f. gathering fresh leaves, a sort of game. —जीव-पत्नी, f. a woman whose hus-band is alive. —जीव-पितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or जीव-पितृक, अस्, आ, अम्, a son or daughter whose father is still alive. —जीव-पीत-सर्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. one whose rays are drunk by living beings; (Sāy.) one whose creation is enjoyed by all. —जीव-पुत्र, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, one whose sons or children are living; (अस्), m. a kind of plant. —जीव-पुत्रक, अस्, m. a tree, commonly Ingua; another plant bearing seeds used in rosaries, commonly Jiyaputa, Nageia Putranjiva. —जीवपुत्र-प्रचायिका, f. the gathering of the above plant, a sort of game. —जीव-पुरा, f., Ved. the abode of living beings or men. —जीव-पुष्प, अम्, n. ‘flower of life,’ N. of a plant and metaphorically applied to the head; N. of two plants, = दमनक and फणिज्झक; (आ), f., N. of a plant, = बृहज्-जीवन्ती. —जीव-प्रिया, f. the tree Terminalia Chebula, = हरीतकी. —जीव-बध, अस्, m. destruction of living beings. —जीव-बर्हिस्, इस्, इस्, इस्, Ved. having a living, i. e. fresh bed of sacrificial grass. —जीव-भद्रा, f. a kind of plant, = जीवन्ती; a kind of medicinal plant, = वृद्धि। —जीव-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become alive, endowed with life. —जीव-भोजन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. giving enjoyment to living beings; (अम्), n. the pleasure or enjoyment of living beings. —जीव-मन्दिर, अम्, n. ‘the mansion of the soul,’ the body. —जीव-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, animated, endowed with life. —जीव-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of an author. —जीव-याज, अस्, m., Ved. the sacrifice of living beings. —जीव-योनि, इस्, इस्, इ, enclosing a soul (as a body or a sentient being). —जीव-रक्त, अम्, n. living blood, menstrual blood. —जीव-रहित, अस्, आ, अम्, lifeless. —जीव-लोक, अस्, m. the world or habitation of living beings (opposed to the world of deceased ancestors), living beings, mankind. —जीव-लौकिक, अस्, आ, अम्, peculiar to the world of living beings or to men. —जीव-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, animated, living; —जीव-वल्ली, f., N. of a plant. —जीव-विचार, अस्, m. title of a Jaina work. —जीवविचार-प्रकरण, अम्, n. title of a Jaina work by Śānti-sūri. —जीव-वृत्ति, इस्, f. breeding or keeping cattle. —जीव-शंस, अस्, m., Ved. rule over living beings; (Sāy.) to be praised by living beings. —जीव-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of an astronomer. —जीव-शाक, अस्, m. a kind of pot-herb growing in Mālava. —जीव-शुक्ला, f. a kind of plant. —जीव-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, one to whom only life is left or who has escaped with his life and nothing more. —जीव-शोणित, अम्, n. living, i. e. healthy blood. —जीव-श्रेष्ठा, f. a kind of medicinal plant. —जीव-सङ्क्रमण, अम्, n. me-tempsychosis. —जीव-सञ्ज्ञ, अस्, m., N. of a shrub, = काम-वृद्धि. —जीव-साधन, अम्, n. ‘means of subsistence,’ rice, grain. —जीव-साफल्य, अम्, n. ‘fruitfulness of life,’ realisation of a life's wishes. —जीव-सुत, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose children are all alive. —जीव-सू, ऊस्, f. the mother of living offspring. —जीव-स्थान, अम्, n. a joint, an articulation. —जीवाजीवाधार (°व-अजीव-आध्°), अस्, m. the world of organic beings and of inorganic matter. —जीवा-जीवाधार-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. the material world, the receptacle of inorganic beings and inorganic substances. —जीवात्मन् (°व-आत्°), आ, m. the living or individual soul enshrined in the human body (distinguished from the परमात्मन् or supreme soul), the vital principle or spirit, that principle of life which renders the body capable of motion or sensation; [cf. जीव।] —जीवा-दान (°व-आद्°), अम्, n. abstracting living or healthy blood, bleeding. —जीवाधान (°व-आध्°), अम्, n. preservation of life. —जीवान्तक (°व-अन्°), अस्, m. a fowler, a birdcatcher; a destroyer of life, a slayer, a murderer. —जीवाभिगम-सूत्र (°व-अभ्°), अम्, n. title of a Jaina work. —जीवाश (°व-आश), अस्, आ, अम्, hoping for life; (आ), f. hope of living. —जीवास्तिकाय (°व-अस्°), अस्, m. (with Jainas) the category of ‘soul.’ —जीवेन्धन (°व-इन्°), अम्, n. glowing fire-wood, burning wood. —जीवोत्सर्ग (°व-उत्°), अस्, m. aban-donment of life, voluntary death. —जीवोर्णा (°व-ऊर्°), f. the wool of a living animal.
जीवक: जीवक, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) living, living by, making a livelihood by, causing to live, generating; one who lives a long time or for whom a long life is desired [cf. आयुष्-मत्]; (अस्), m. a living being; a servant, slave, one who makes a livelihood by service; a mendicant, one who lives by begging; an usurer, one who lives by lending money at high interest; a snake-catcher, one whose business is to catch snakes and cure their bites &c.; a tree; N. of several plants, = Terminalia Tomentosa, Coccinia Grandis, a cucurbitaceous plant; a medicinal plant, commonly called by the same name Jīvaka and con-sidered as one of the eight principal drugs classed together under the name Aṣṭa-varga; N. of a man; (इका), f. the living or life-giving element (i. e. water); living, means of living, livelihood; N. of a plant, = जीवन्ती; [cf. अज-जीवक।]
जीवत्: जीवत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, living, alive; जीवन्न् एव, during life. —जीवत्-तोका, f. a woman whose children are living. —जीवत्-पति, इस्, or जीवत्-पत्नी, f. a wife whose husband is alive. —जीवत्-पितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or जीवत्-पितृक, अस्, आ, अम्, a son or daughter whose father is alive; [cf. जीव-पितृ।] —जीवत्पितृक-निर्णय, अस्, m. title of a work by Rāma-kṛṣṇa. —जीवन्-मुक्त, अस्, m. a man purified by knowledge of Brahma and exonerated whilst living from future birth and all ritual ceremonies. —जीवन्-मुक्ति, इस्, f. libera-tion in the present state of life. In the Vedānta system a secondary sort of liberation which conducts the soul after death to live with Brahma, not however divested of a subtile corporeal frame. —जीवन्मुक्ति-विवेक, अस्, m. title of a philosophical treatise. —जीवन्-मृत, अस्, आ, अम्, at once alive and dead, dead while alive, (said of one whose character is lost or of a madman &c.)
जीवथ: जीवथ, अस्, आ, अम्, long-lived; virtuous, pious; (अस्), m. life, existence, breath; a tortoise; a pea-cock; a cloud; virtue, piety.
जीवन: जीवन, अस्, ई, अम्, enlivening, vivifying, giving life; (अस्), m. a living being, an animal; wind; a son; a kind of drug, = जीवक; N. of a plant, = क्षुद्र-फलक; N. of the author of the work Mānasa-nayana; (आ), f. a kind of medicinal plant; (ई), f., N. of several plants and drugs, = जीवन्ती, काकोली, a kind of jasmine &c.; (अम्), n. life, existence, living, livelihood, profession (often at the end of a comp., e. g. मृग-जीवन, living by hunting); en-livening, making alive; the life-giving element (water); butter made from new milk or milk one day old; mar-row. —जीवन-ता, f. life, mode of life. —जीवन-योनि, इस्, m. source of life. —जीवन-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of or relating to life. —जीवन-विडम्बन, अम्, n. disappointment in life, living in vain. —जीवन-हेतु, उस्, m. object of life, cause of living. —जीवना-घात (°न-आघ्°), अम्, n. ‘that which destroys life,’ poison. —जीवनान्त (°न-अन्°), अस्, m. end of life, death. —जीवनावास (°न-आव्°), अस्, m. Varuṇa, the regent of water. —जीवनोपाय (°न-उप्°), अस्, m. livelihood, means of subsistence. —जीवनौषध (°न-औष्°), अम्, n. an invigorating or life-giving medicine, a drug for reviving the dead; elixir vitæ.
जीवनक: जीवनक, अस्, इका, अम्, enlivening; (अम्), n. food; (इका), f. the tree Terminalia Chebula, = हरीतकी।
जीवनस्या: जीवनस्या, f., Ved. desire of life.
जीवनीय: जीवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be lived; supporting life, N. of a particular class of drugs; (आ), f. a kind of plant, = जीवन्ती; (अम्), n. a form of milk, milk fresh from the cow; water.
जीवन्त: जीवन्त, अस्, ई, अम्, living, existent, long-lived; (अस्), m. life, existence; a medicament, a drug; a kind of pot-herb (जीव-शाक); N. of a man; (ई), f. a kind of medicinal plant, also eaten as a vegetable, = Pæderia Fœtida (?); also = गुडूची, Cocculus Cor-difolius and = वन्दा, a parasitical plant.
जीवन्तिक: जीवन्तिक, अस्, m. a fowler, a birdcatcher; see जीवान्तक; (इका), f. a parasitical plant, Epidendron Tesseloides, and other species; a plant Menispermum Glabrum; a kind of pot-herb.
जीवमान: जीवमान, अस्, आ, अम्, living, alive.
जीवल: जीवल, अस्, आ, अम्, full of life, animating; (अस्), m. a kind of plant; N. of a man; (आ), f. a kind of plant.
जीवातु: जीवातु, उस्, f. life, existence; (उस्, उ), m. n. victuals, food, boiled rice; a medicine for restoring life; [cf. Lat. victus.] —जीवातु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, animated, living.
जीविका: जीविका, see under जीवक. —जीविकापन्न (°का-आप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having obtained subsistence. —जीवि-का-प्राप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having obtained a livelihood.
जीवित: जीवित, अस्, आ, अम्, lived, lived through (as a period of time), living, alive, existent; revivified, returned to life; animated, enlivened; (अम्), n. a living being; living, life, existence; duration of life; livelihood, means of existence; [cf. Lith. gywata; Slav. schi-vot; Lat. vita for vivita.] —जीवित-काल, अस्, m. life-time, period or duration of life, a life. —जीवित-ज्ञा, f. an artery, a vessel of the body. —जीवित-नाथ, अस्, m. ‘lord of life,’ a husband. —जीवित-योपन, अस्, आ, अम्, oppressing or molesting living beings. —जीवित-व्यय, अस्, m. casting away life, sacrifice of life. —जीवित-संशय, अस्, m. risk of life, fear of death. —जीवित-हारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, de-stroying life. —जीवितान्त (°त-अन्°), अस्, m. end of life, death. —जीवितान्तक (°त-अन्°), अस्, m. putting an end to life, an epithet of Śiva. —जीविताशा (°त-आशा), f. hope of life; love of life. —जीवितेप्सु (°त-ईप्°), उस्, उस्, उ, seeking to save (one's) life. —जीवितेश (°त-ईश), अस्, आ, अम्, presiding over life; (अस्), m. ‘the lord or master of existence,’ a lover, a husband; an epithet of Yama the regent of death; the sun; the moon; a drug to revive the dead. —जीवितेश्वर (°त-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of life,’ an epithet of Śiva.
जीवितव्य: जीवितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be lived, to be kept alive; (अम्), n. the possibility of living; possible return to life.
जीविन्: जीविन्, ई, इनी, इ, living, alive, animate; living upon or by; (ई), m. a living being. —जीवि-त्व, अम्, n. life, existence.

जेह्: जेह् जेह् (related to 1. जभ् and जृभ्), cl. 1. A., Ved. जेहते, जिजेहे, जेहिष्यते, जेहितुम्, to open the mouth, breathe heavily, gasp, gape, open wide, yawn; (Sāy.) to reach, go towards, strive after: Caus. जेहयति, अजिजेहत्।
जेहमान: जेहमान, अस्, आ, अम्, gaping, opening wide; (Sāy.) going towards.
जै: जै जै, cl. 1. P. जायति, जजौ, जास्यति, जा-तुम्, to wane, decline, fade away, perish; [cf. 1. ज्या।]
जैगीषव्य: जैगीषव्य जैगीषव्य, अस्, m. (fr. जिगीषु), N. of an ancient Ṛṣi often named in connection with Asita Devala. —जैगीषव्येश्वर (°य-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga in Vārāṇasī.
जैत्र: जैत्र जैत्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. rt. 1. जि), victorious, triumphant, leading to victory, overcoming, surpass-ing, superior; (अस्), m. a conqueror, victor; N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (ई), f. the plant Sesbania Ægyptiaca; (अम्), n. victory, triumph, superiority. —जैत्र-रथ, अस्, आ, अम्, having a triumphant car; (अस्), m. a victor, a conqueror, a hero; a triumphant car.
जैत्रायणि: जैत्रायणि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Jaitra.
जैन: जैन जैन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जिन), relating to the Jinas; (अस्), m. a Jaina, a teacher of heterodox notions, the chief of which are the supremacy of certain Jinas or great saints over the gods of the Hindūs, a denial of the divine authority of the Vedas, and a disregard of the distinction of castes; N. of a prince of Kaśmīra. —जैन-तरङ्गिणी, f. a history of Kaśmīra by Śrīvara. —जैनाश्रम (°न-आश्°), अस्, m. a Jaina monastery. —जैनेन्द्र (°न-इन्°), अस्, m., N. of a grammarian.
जैन्य: जैन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the Jainas (?).
जैपाल: जैपाल जैपाल, अस्, m. (= जय-पाल), a plant, Croton Tiglium.
जैमन्त: जैमन्त जैमन्त, अस्, m., N. of a man.
जैमन्तायन: जैमन्तायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Jai-manta.
जैमिनि: जैमिनि जैमिनि, इस्, m., N. of a celebrated saint and philosopher, the pupil of Vyāsa and founder of the Pūrva (or Karma) Mimāṃsā school. He is said to have acted as Udgātṛ at the sacrifice of Janam-ejaya (Mahā-bh. I. 2046), and to have received the Sāma-veda from Vyāsa.
जैमिनीय: जैमिनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to Jaimini; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school of the Sāma-veda.
जैमूत: जैमूत जैमूत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जीमूत), relating to Jīmūta.
जैयट: जैयट जैयट, अस्, m., N. of the father of Kaiyaṭa; (sometimes spelt जैगट।)
जैय्यट: जैय्यट, अस्, m., N. of a physician.
जैव: जैव जैव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जीव), relating to Jupiter.
जैवन्तायन: जैवन्तायन, अस्, m. or जैवन्तायनि, इस्, m. or जैवन्ति, इस्, m. a patronymic from Jīvanta.
जैवलि: जैवलि, इस्, m. (fr. जीवल), a patronymic of Pra-vāhana.
जैवातृक: जैवातृक, अस्, ई, अम्, long-lived, one for whom long life is desired; thin, lean; (अस्), m. the moon; camphor (as a synonym of the moon); a peasant; a drug, medicament; a son; [cf. जीवातु।]
जैवि: जैवि, इस्, m. or जैवेय, अस्, m. a patronymic from Jīva.
जैष्णव: जैष्णव जैष्णव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जिष्णु), re-lating to a conqueror, relating to Arjuna.
जैह्मय: जैह्मय जैह्म्य, अम्, n. (fr. जिह्म), crooked-ness (moral or physical), deceit, falsehood.
जैह्व: जैह्व जैह्व, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जिह्वा), belonging or relating to the tongue, lying on the tongue.
जैह्वाकात: जैह्वाकात, अस्, ई, अम्, an adj. derived fr. जिह्वा-कात्य।
जैह्व्य: जैह्व्य, अम्, n. the pleasure of taste (derived from the tongue), pleasure.
जोगू: जोगू जोगू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ (fr. rt. गु), Ved. praising.
जोङ्ग: जोङ्ग जोङ्ग or जोङ्गक, अम्, n. aloe wood, Agallochum.
जोङ्गट: जोङ्गट जोङ्गट, अस्, m. longing, earnest wish, eager desire, the longing of a pregnant woman.
जोटिङ्ग: जोटिङ्ग जोटिङ्ग, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva; a devotee, an ascetic who subjects himself to the severest penances; the sacrificial cord (?).
जोनराज: जोनराज जोन-राज, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Rāja-taraṅgiṇī.
जोन्नाला: जोन्नाला जोन्नाला, f. = यवनाल, the plant Andropogon Saccharatus; also जोन्ताला।
जोल: जोल जोल, N. of a mixed caste.
जोषण: जोषण, अम्, n. liking; satisfaction, approval; choosing; (आ), f. the expression of satisfaction by the word जुष्।
जोषयितव्य: जोषयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be made dear or agreeable, to be reflected upon or thought about, obscure, unintelligible (in words).
जोषयितृ: जोषयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or जोष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, loving, cherishing, fostering, taking care of; (Sāy.) serving.
जोषस्: जोषस् in वि-जोषस्, स-जोषस्, q. v.
जोष्य: जोष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. delightful, agreeable, wel-come, satisfactory.
जोषा: जोषा जोषा, f. = योषा, a woman.
जोषिका: जोषिका जोषिका, f. = जालिका, a cluster of young buds, a bud, a germ.
जोषित्: जोषित् जोषित् or जोषिता, f. = योषित्, a woman.
जोहूत्र: जोहूत्र जोहूत्र, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. ह्वे), Ved. making a loud noise, neighing; calling out, challeng-ing to battle, neighing (as a horse).
जौमर: जौमर जौमर, अम्, n., scil. व्या-करण, the grammar composed by Jumara.
जौलायनभक्त: जौलायनभक्त जौलायन-भक्त, अम्, n. the district inhabited by the Jaulāyanas.
जौहोत्यादिक: जौहोत्यादिक जौहोत्यादिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जुहोत्य्-आदि), belonging to the class of roots begin-ning with हु, i. e. to the third class.
ज्ञ: ज्ञ 1. ज्ञ = ज्ञु = जानु, the knee, in ऊर्-ध्व-ज्ञ। (For 2. ज्ञ see below.)

2. ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, who or what knows, a knower, knowing, familiar with (often in comp., e. g. धर्म-ज्ञ, familiar with the law; सर्व-ज्ञ, knowing everything); intelligent, wise; (अस्), m. a wise and learned man, especially one possessed of sacred learn-ing or religious knowledge; the sentient soul; Budha who was first of the lunar line and regent of the planet Mercury; the planet Mars or its regent; an epithet of Brahmā; [cf. Lat. beni-gnus, mali-gnus.] —ज्ञ-ता, f. (at the end of a comp.) knowledge of, familiarity with; intelligence. —ज्ञम्मन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, think-ing one's self wise.
ज्ञा: ज्ञा 1. ज्ञा, cl. 9. P. A. जानाति, जानीते, ज-ज्ञौ, जज्ञे, ज्ञास्यति, -ते, अज्ञासीत्, अज्ञास्त, ज्ञातुम्, [irreg. forms, जानथ for जानीथ Mahā-bh. II. 842, जानत for जानीत II. 2397, जिजाहि for जाज्ञाहि = जानीहि, know thou, XIII. 4495, अभ्य्-अनु-जानिथास् for अभ्य्-अन्व्-अजानीथास् XIV. 1641, जान-मान pres. part.], to know, have knowledge, become acquainted with; to perceive, apprehend, understand, experience; to recognise; to ascertain, investigate; to know as, know or perceive that, regard or consider as (with acc. of the object and predicate, e. g. तस्य मां तनयां जानीत, know me to be his daughter); to be conversant or familiar with; to visit as a friend (Ved.); to acknowledge, approve, allow, permit; to recognise as one's own, take possession of; to act, en-gage in (with gen. of the instrument, e. g. सर्पिषो for सर्पिषा जानीते, he engages in sacrifice with clarified butter): Caus. ज्ञापयति or ज्ञपयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अजिज्ञपत्, to make known, teach, make acquainted with, inform, announce, notify; to give information; A. to request, ask: Desid. A. जिज्ञासते (ep. also P.), to wish to know, &c.; to investigate, examine, wish to learn; to conjecture, suppose: Desid. of Caus. जिज्ञापयिषति and जिज्ञपयिषति and ज्ञीप्सति, to wish to make known or inform: Pass. of Desid. of Caus. ज्ञीप्स्यते, to be wished or intended to be in-formed: Intens. जाज्ञायते, जाज्ञाति, जाज्ञेति; [cf. Lat. gna, gno, in gnârus, (g)nosco, cognosco, ignoro; perhaps gloria for gnoria: Gr. γνω in γνῶθι, ἔγνων, γνῶσις; (γ)νοέω, (γ)νοῦς; γιγνώ-σκω: Old Germ. chna, chnâta, chnât: Eng. know: Goth. kaun: Old Germ. chan: Germ. kann, kenne: Lith. zinnaù, ‘I know;’ zinne, sazinne: Slav. najû: Hib. gnia, ‘knowledge;’ gnic; gno, ‘ingenious;’ gnas, ‘custom, use.’]

2. ज्ञा, आस्, आस्, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) know-ing, familiar with [cf. ऋत-ज्ञा, पद-ज्ञा, and 2. ज्ञ]; (आ), f. in epic poetry sometimes a shortened form of आ-ज्ञा, the initial vowel of the latter being irregularly elided after a preceding final ए and ओ (e. g. तेऽज्ञया, by thy order, Mahā-bh. 1. 3168).
ज्ञक: ज्ञक, अस्, अका or इका, m. f. a diminutive fr. 2. ज्ञ।
ज्ञपित: ज्ञपित, अस्, आ, अम्, made known, informed, taught, expounded.
ज्ञप्त: ज्ञप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, made known, = ज्ञपित।
ज्ञप्ति: ज्ञप्ति, इस्, f. understanding, apprehension, the exercise of the intellectual faculty; promulgating, making known.
ज्ञात: ज्ञात, अस्, आ, अम्, known, ascertained, compre-hended, perceived, understood; आं ज्ञातम्, Ah! I know (lit. it is known). —ज्ञात-नन्दन, अस्, m. an epithet of Vīra, the twenty-fourth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī. —ज्ञात-मात्रे, ind. on its being ascertained merely. —ज्ञात-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m. a man completely versed in any science or Śāstra. —ज्ञाताधर्म-कथा (°त-अध्° or °ता-ध° ?), f. title of one of the twelve sacred books of the Jainas. —ज्ञातान्वय (°त-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘of known lineage,’ a name of Vardhamāna, the last Jina or Jaina pontiff.
ज्ञातक: ज्ञातक, अस्, आ, अम्, known, &c. See ज्ञात।
ज्ञातल: ज्ञातल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
ज्ञातलेय: ज्ञातलेय, अस्, m. a patronymic from the last.
ज्ञातव्य: ज्ञातव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be known or understood, to be investigated or inquired after; perceptible, con-ceivable; to be considered as.
ज्ञाति: ज्ञाति, इस्, m. a paternal relation, a kinsman in ge-neral, a father, a brother; a distant kinsman, one who does not participate in the oblations offered to de-ceased ancestors; (इस्), f., N. of a woman; (according to the Schol. ज्ञाति is a paternal, and सम्-बन्धिन् a maternal relation; the original meaning of ज्ञाति may be ‘intimately acquainted;’ cf. Gr. γνωτός, γνωτή; Goth. knôdi.) —ज्ञाति-कर्मन्, अ, n. or ज्ञाति-कार्य, अम्, n. the act or duty of a kinsman. —ज्ञाति-त्व, अम्, n. relationship, consanguinity. —ज्ञाति-द्रव्य-विनाकृत, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of relations and wealth. —ज्ञाति-पुत्र, अस्, m. the son of a relative; an epithet of Pūrṇa. —ज्ञाति-भाव, अस्, m. the condition of a kinsman, relationship, kin. —ज्ञाति-भेद, अस्, m. dissension among relatives. —ज्ञाति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has near rela-tions. —ज्ञाति-मुख, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the appearance or character of a relative. —ज्ञाति-विद्, त्, त्, त्, one who has or makes near relations.
ज्ञातृ: ज्ञातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, knowing, wise, intelligent, a knower; (ता), m. an acquaintance; a bail, a surety; [cf. Gr. γνωστήρ.] —ज्ञातृ-त्व, अम्, n. or ज्ञातृ-ता, f. knowledge, information.
ज्ञात्र: ज्ञात्र, अम्, n., Ved. the faculty of perception, intelligence, knowledge.
ज्ञात्वा: ज्ञात्वा, ind. having known, having ascertained, &c.
ज्ञान: ज्ञान, अम्, n. knowing, understanding, becoming acquainted with, knowledge; sacred or religious knowledge, especially that which is derived from meditation on the higher truths of religion and philosophy and which teaches man his own nature and how he may be reunited to the supreme spirit; knowledge about anything, cognizance, consciousness (e. g. तस्य ज्ञानात्, with his knowledge; अ-ज्ञानात् तस्य, without his knowledge or cognizance; ज्ञा-नाद् अ-ज्ञानाद् वा, knowingly or ignorantly; विगत-ज्ञान, one who has lost consciousness); conscience; organ of intelligence, sense. —ज्ञान-कन्द, अस्, m., N. of a pupil of Śaṅkarācārya. —ज्ञान-काण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. that inner or esoteric portion of the Veda which relates to true spiritual knowledge or the knowledge of the supreme spirit as distinguished from the knowledge of ceremonies; [cf. कर्म-काण्ड।] —ज्ञान-कीर्त्ति, इस्, m., N. of a Buddhist preceptor. —ज्ञान-केतु, उस्, m. a mark of intelli-gence; (उस्, उस्, उ), furnished with marks of in-telligence. —ज्ञानकेतु-ध्वज, अस्, m., N. of a divine being. —ज्ञान-खण्ड, title of a part of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —ज्ञान-गम्य, अस्, आ, अम्, attainable by the understanding. —ज्ञान-गर्भ, अस्, m. ‘filled with knowledge,’ N. of a scholar; also of a Bodhi-sattva. —ज्ञान-चक्षुस्, उस्, n. the eye of intelligence, inner eye, mind's eye, intellectual vision. —ज्ञान-तत्त्व, अम्, n. true knowledge, knowledge of God. —ज्ञान-तपस्, अस्, n. penance consisting in the cul-tivation of true knowledge. —ज्ञान-तस्, ind. know-ingly, intuitively, designedly; ज्ञानतोऽज्ञानतो वा, knowingly or unknowingly. —ज्ञान-द, अस्, m. an imparter of knowledge. —ज्ञान-दत्त, अस्, m. ‘given by knowledge,’ N. of a scholar. —ज्ञान-दर्पण, अस्, m. ‘mirror of true knowledge,’ a N. of Mañju-śrī. —ज्ञान-दीप, अस्, m. the lamp of knowledge, knowledge. —ज्ञान-दुर्बल, अस्, आ, अम्, de-ficient in knowledge, ignorant. —ज्ञान-निश्चय, अस्, m. soundness of knowledge, certainty, ascertain-ment. —ज्ञान-निष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, engaged in cultivating true knowledge. —ज्ञानपत, अस्, ई, अम्, an adj. derived from the next. —ज्ञान-पति, इस्, m. the lord of knowledge. —ज्ञान-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, versed in spiritual wisdom. —ज्ञान-पावन, अस्, आ, अम्, purifying knowledge, refining the understanding; (अम्), n., N. of a Tīrtha. —ज्ञान-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, preceded by knowledge or wisdom. —ज्ञान-प्र-काश, अस्, m. title of a poem by Jagajjīvana-dāsa. —ज्ञान-प्रदीप, अस्, m. title of the second book of the Yoga-sāra-saṅgraha. —ज्ञान-प्रभ, अस्, m., N. of a man; also of a Bodhi-sattva. —ज्ञान-प्र-वाद, अम्, n. title of one of the fourteen Pūrvas or older writings of the Jainas. —ज्ञान-प्रस्थान, अम्, n. ‘system or method of knowledge,’ title of a Buddhist work. —ज्ञान-बोधिनी, f. ‘awakening knowledge,’ title of a philosophical treatise composed by Śaṅkara. —ज्ञान-भास्कर, अस्, m. ‘sun of knowledge,’ title of a medical compilation. —ज्ञान-मण्डप, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘temple of knowledge,’ N. of a temple. —ज्ञान-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of knowledge, containing knowledge. —ज्ञान-मुक्तावली, f. ‘necklace of knowledge,’ title of an astronomical work. —ज्ञान-मुद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having the impress of wisdom, wise. —ज्ञान-मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, founded on spiritual knowledge. —ज्ञान-मेरु, उस्, m., N. of a man. —ज्ञान-रत्नावली, f. title of a book. —ज्ञान-राज, अस्, m. ‘king of know-ledge,’ N. of the author of the Siddhānta-sundara. —ज्ञानर्षि-भास्कराचार्य (°न-ऋष्°, °र-आच्°), अस्, m., N. of an author. —ज्ञान-लक्षण, अम्, आ, n. f. indication, sign, means of knowing or inferring; (in logic) sign or proof or characteristic of knowledge; subsequent derived from antecedent knowledge. —ज्ञान-वज्र, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist author. —ज्ञान-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, endowed with knowledge or science, knowing, familiar with, intelligent, wise, learned, having spiritual knowledge; (आन्), m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva. —ज्ञान-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a poet. —ज्ञान-वापी, f. ‘pool of divine knowledge,’ N. of a Tīrtha. —ज्ञान-विज्ञान, अम्, n. sacred and miscellaneous knowledge; the Vedas with the sup-plementary branches of knowledge, medicine, arms, &c. —ज्ञान-विभूति-गर्भ, अस्, m. ‘filled with superhuman knowledge,’ N. of a Bodhi-sattva. —ज्ञान-विलास-काव्य, अम्, n. title of a poem. —ज्ञान-शक्ति, इस्, f. capacity of knowing. —ज्ञा-न-शास्त्र, अम्, n. ‘the science of knowing the future,’ a manual of fortune-telling. —ज्ञान-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, pre-eminent in wisdom. —ज्ञा-न-हस्तिक, अस्, m., N. of a man. —ज्ञानाकर (°न-आक्°), अस्, m. ‘mine of knowledge,’ N. of a son of Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū; N. of a Buddha. —ज्ञानात्मन् (°न-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, all-wise. —ज्ञानानन्द (°न-आन्°), अस्, m. ‘joy of know-ledge,’ N. of an author. —ज्ञानानुत्पाद (°न-अन्°), अस्, m. non-production of knowledge, folly, ignorance. —ज्ञानामृत (°न-अम्°), अम्, n. ‘nectar of knowledge,’ title of a grammar. —ज्ञानार्णव (°न-अर्°), अस्, m. ‘ocean of knowledge,’ title of a manual of medicine composed by Yama-rāja; title of a prayer-book. —ज्ञानावरणीय (°न-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, to be covered or obstructed by knowledge, (an act which is considered) to be impeded by knowledge; also written ज्ञानवरणीय. —ज्ञानावलोकालङ्का-र (°न-अवलोक-अल्°), अस्, m. title of a Buddhist work. —ज्ञानावस्थित (°न-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, engaged in cultivating wisdom. —ज्ञानेन्द्र-सरस्वती (°न-इन्°), m., N. of a scholiast on the Siddhānta-kaumudī. —ज्ञानेन्द्रिय (°न-इन्°), अम्, n. an organ of per-ception or sensation, of which there are five, viz. the skin, tongue, eye, ear, and nose; see इन्द्रिय। —ज्ञानोद-तीर्थ (°न-उद्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha; ‘the Tīrtha of the waters of knowledge.’ —ज्ञानोल्का (°न-उल्°), f. ‘the meteor of know-ledge,’ N. of a Samādhi.
ज्ञानिक: ज्ञानिक, अस्, आ, अम्, at the end of comp. = ज्ञान।
ज्ञानिन्: ज्ञानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, endowed with knowledge or intelligence, intelligent, wise, a knower; (ई), f. an astrologer, a fortune-teller, a man prescient of future events; a sage, one possessing religious wisdom. —ज्ञानि-त्व, अम्, n. prescience, fortune-telling.
ज्ञानीय: ज्ञानीय, nom. P. ज्ञानीयति, -यितुम्, to wish for knowledge.
ज्ञापक: ज्ञापक, अस्, आ, अम्, making or causing to know, teaching, designing, informing; (अस्), m. a teacher, an instructor; a commander, a master; a master of requests, an officer of the court of a Hindū prince; (अम्), n. a significant expression or one which gives some particular information, a precept, a rule, a name given to those rules of Pāṇini which imply or indi-cate some other grammatical laws than those which would follow from the mere words of the Jñāpaka rules themselves. —ज्ञापक-समुच्चय, अस्, m. a work by Puruṣottama-deva giving a collection of the Jñāpaka rules contained in Pāṇini's grammar.
ज्ञापन: ज्ञापन, अम्, n. making known, announcing, apprizing, informing, teaching, notification.
ज्ञापनीय: ज्ञापनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be made known or announced.
ज्ञापित: ज्ञापित, अस्, आ, अम्, made known, informed.
ज्ञाप्ति: ज्ञाप्ति, इस्, f. making known, apprizing, informing.
ज्ञाप्य: ज्ञाप्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be made known or in-formed, to be told.
ज्ञास्: ज्ञास्, m., Ved. a near relative; [cf. ज्ञाति।]
ज्ञीप्स्यमान: ज्ञीप्स्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being intended to be informed.
ज्ञेय: ज्ञेय, अस्, आ, अम्, cognizable, to be ascertained or investigated, to be learned or understood, to be per-ceived or inquired about; to be regarded as. —ज्ञेय-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, understanding what is to be under-stood; the mind. —ज्ञेय-ता, f. or ज्ञेय-त्व, अम्, n. perceptibility, intelligibleness.
ज्ञु: ज्ञु ज्ञु = जानु, the knee, in अभि-ज्ञु, ऊर्-ध्व-ज्ञु, &c. —ज्ञु-बाध्, -भात्, त्, त्, Ved. bending the knees; [cf. Gr. πρόχνυ.]
ज्मन्: ज्मन् ज्मन् (fr. जम् = गम्), only occurring in the Ved. loc. ज्मन्, in (his) course or way; (Sāy.) in the sky; on the earth; [cf. उरु-ज्मन् and पृथु-ज्मन्।] —ज्म-या, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. going on or following a course; (Sāy.) on the earth (as if ज्मया).
ज्मायत्: ज्मायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (pres. part. of a nom. fr. ज्मन्), Ved. making a way or course; (Sāy.) going on or reaching the earth.
ज्या: ज्या 1. ज्या, cl. 9. P., 4. A. जिनाति, जीयते, जिज्यौ, जिज्ये, ज्यास्यति, -ते, अज्यासीत्, ज्या-तुम्, to overpower, oppress, to deprive of property, &c., (in the Veda often connected with rt. हन्, e. g. जीयते हन्ति, ‘he oppresses and kills;’ and in the Brāhmaṇas applied to the oppressions of the Brāhmans and Vaiśyas by the Kṣatriyas); (cl. 4. A.) to be oppressed, treated badly, deprived of property, &c.; (cl. 9. P.) to become old: Caus. ज्यापयति, see ज्यापय below: Desid. P. जिज्यासति, to wish to over-power or oppress: Intens. जेजीयते, जाज्याति; [cf. Gr. βιάω.]
2. ज्या, f. overpowering force or strength (βία, cf. परम-ज्या); excessive demand, importunity.

ज्या 3. ज्या, f. (perhaps fr. rt. 1. ज्या), the string of a bow, a bow-string; the chord of an arc, a sine in geometry; [cf. अधि-ज्य, उज्-ज्य, &c.; cf. also Gr. βιός.] —ज्या-कार, अस्, m., Ved. one who makes bow-strings. —ज्या-घोष, अस्, m. the twang of a bow. —ज्या-पाश, अस्, m. a bow-string. —ज्या-पिण्ड or ज्या-पिण्डक, a sine expressed in figures. —ज्या-मघ, अस्, m., N. of the father of Vi-darbha. —ज्यार्ध (ज्या-अर्°), अस्, m. the sine of an arc. —ज्यार्ध-पिण्ड, a sine expressed in figures. —ज्या-वाज, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the elasticity of a bow-string; (Sāy.) a stout or strong bow (as if a substantive). —ज्या-वाणेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a warrior-tribe; (अस्), m. a prince of this tribe. —ज्या-ह्रोड, अस्, m. a peculiar kind of bow; (औ), m. du., N. of a Sāman. —ज्योत्पत्ति (ज्या-उत्°), इस्, f. ‘the calculation of the length of a chord,’ derivation of (semi)-chords.
ज्या 4. ज्या, f. the earth; a mother.
ज्य: ज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) oppressing.
ज्यान: ज्यान, अम्, n., Ved. oppression, tyrannizing over.
ज्यानि: ज्यानि, इस्, f. oppression; deprivation, loss; decay, infirmity, old age; quitting, abandoning; a river, a stream.
ज्यापय: ज्यापय, nom. P. ज्यापयति, -यितुम्, to make old, to call a person old, (supposed to be a nom. fr. ज्य substituted for वृद्ध।)
ज्यायस्: ज्यायस्, आन्, असी, अस् (considered by grammarians to be a compar. of प्र-शस्य and वृद्ध, for which ज्य is substituted), superior, more excellent, greater, larger, stronger; elder, senior, elder born (opposed to कनीयस् and अणीयस्); a master; most excellent; (in law) one who is of age and answerable for his own conduct. —ज्यायस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having or acknowledging a senior or superior.
ज्यायस: ज्यायस, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. greater in number (op-posed to कानीयस).
ज्यायिष्ठ: ज्यायिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (irreg. superl.), the most excellent; noblest, first, best.
ज्येय: ज्येय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be oppressed, to be deprived of (property &c.); the most excellent, first, best.
ज्येष्ठ: ज्येष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, the most excellent, noblest, pre-eminent; first, chief; best, greatest; eldest, very old, elder, senior, elder born; an elder brother; (अस्), m., N. of a month, for ज्यैष्ठ, q. v.; N. of a man; (आ), f., N. of the sixteenth or (according to more modern reckoning) eighteenth lunar mansion sacred to Indra; the eighth year of a Jupiter cycle of twelve years; the middle finger; a small house-lizard; an epithet of the Gaṅgā; a kind of heroine; misfortune personified as a goddess and the elder sister of Lakṣmī; (ई), f. a small house-lizard; (अम्), n. the most excellent, the first, the head; tin; (अम्), ind. most, extremely; [cf. Hib. gast, ‘an old woman;’ giostaire, ‘an active old man;’ giostai-reas, ‘old age.’] —ज्येष्ठ-घ्नी, f., Ved. = ज्ये-ष्ठा, the sixteenth lunar mansion. —ज्येष्ठ-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. best of all; first of all; oldest of all. —ज्येष्ठ-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, elder, an elder one. —ज्येष्ठ-तस्, ind., Ved. according to seniority, (reckoning) from the eldest. —ज्येष्ठ-ता, f. or ज्येष्ठ-त्व, अम्, n. superiority; primogeniture, seniority. —ज्येष्ठ-तात, अस्, m. a father's elder brother. —ज्येष्ठ-ताति, इस्, f., Ved. superiority; superior. —ज्येष्ठ-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man. —ज्येष्ठ-पुष्कर, अम्, n., N. of a renowned place of pilgrimage. —ज्येष्ठ-बला, f., N. of a plant, a kind of Balā, = महा-बला, सह-देवी। —ज्येष्ठ-भार्या, f. an elder brother's wife, the elder, senior or chief wife. —ज्येष्ठ-राज्, ट्, m., Ved. a sovereign. —ज्येष्ठ-ललिता, f. a particular vow to be observed in the month Jyeṣṭha (Jyaiṣṭha). —ज्येष्ठ-वर्ण, अस्, m. one of the first caste, a Brāhman. —ज्येष्ठ-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, behaving like the first-born or eldest brother; (इस्), f. the duties of seniority. —ज्येष्ठ-श्वश्रू, ऊस्, f. a wife's elder sister. —ज्येष्ठ-सामन्, अ, n., N. of a Sāman; (आ, आ, अ), a chanter of the Jyeṣṭha-Sāman. —ज्ये-ष्ठसामिक, अस्, आ, अम्, an adj. derived from the last. —ज्येष्ठ-स्तोम, अस्, m., N. of an Ekāha ceremony. —ज्येष्ठ-स्थान, अम्, n., N. of a place of pilgrimage. —ज्येष्ठांश (°ठ-अं°), अस्, m. the eldest brother's share; the right of primogeniture or the right of the eldest son to a larger portion of the patrimonial property than his brothers, — a right formerly recognized but now obsolete; the best share. —ज्येष्ठा-मूल or ज्येष्ठा-मूलीय, अस्, m. the month Jyaiṣṭha. —ज्येष्ठाम्बु (°ठ-अम्°), उस्, m. the scum of boiled rice or water in which grain has been washed. —ज्येष्ठाश्रम (°ठ-आश्°), अस्, m. the most excellent order or period in the religious life of a Brāhman, viz. that of a householder; (अस्, आ, अम्), being in that period. —ज्येष्ठाश्रमिन्, ई, m. a Brāhman in the order of a householder. —ज्ये-ष्ठेश्वर (°ठ-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga in Vārāṇasī.
ज्येष्ठिला: ज्येष्ठिला, f., N. of a river.
ज्यैष्ठ: ज्यैष्ठ, अस्, m., N. of a month (May — June), the month in which the full moon stands in the constellation Jyeṣṭhā; (ई), f. the full moon in the month Jyaiṣṭha; a small house-lizard. —ज्यैष्ठ-सामन्, a wrong form for ज्येष्ठ-सामन्, q. v.
ज्यैष्ठिनेय: ज्यैष्ठिनेय, अस्, ई, अम्, born from the elder or principal wife; ज्यैष्ठिनेयो ज्येष्ठः, the eldest son and at the same time the son of the father's first wife.
ज्यैष्ठ्य: ज्यैष्ठ्य, अम्, n. pre-eminence, sovereignty; pre-cedence, priority of birth, primogeniture, seniority.
ज्यका: ज्यका, f. a bow-string; the chord of an arc in geometry.
ज्याय: ज्याय, nom. A. ज्यायते, to represent a bow-string.
ज्यु: ज्यु ज्यु, cl. 1. A. ज्यवते, &c., to go, approach.
ज्युत्: ज्युत् ज्युत् (for द्युत्), cl. 1. A. P. ज्योतते, -ति, to shine: Caus. P. ज्योतयति, -यितुम्, to shine upon, illuminate.
ज्युति: ज्युति, इस्, f. (for द्युति), light. —ज्युति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, shining, full of light.
ज्योता: ज्योता, f., Ved. ‘the brilliant or shining one,’ one of the mystical names of the cow.
ज्योतिष: ज्योतिष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. ज्योतिस्), relating to the heavenly bodies, astronomical, astrological; (अस्), m. an astronomer, astrologer; N. of certain magical formularies for exorcising the evil spirits supposed to possess weapons; (अम्), n. astronomy, astrology, the science of the course of the heavenly bodies and divi-sions of time resting thereon; N. of one of the six Vedāṅgas or of a short tract which gives only such a knowledge of the heavenly bodies as was required for fixing the days and hours of the Vedic sacrifices; (ई), f. a star, a planet, an asterism. —ज्यो-तिष-तत्त्व, अम्, n. or ज्योतिष-रत्नमाला, f., N. of two works on astronomy. —ज्योतिष-विद्या, f. astro-nomical science. —ज्योतिष-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. the whole science of astronomy. —ज्योतिषी-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. shining, brilliant; (आन्), m., N. of a par-ticular sun or form of the sun.
ज्योतिषिक: ज्योतिषिक, a wrong form for ज्यौतिषिक, q. v.
ज्योतिष्क: ज्योतिष्क, अस्, m. a luminary, a heavenly body; the luminaries regarded by the Jainas as a class of deities arranged under five heads, viz. sun, moon, the planets, fixed stars, and lunar mansions; the plant Premna Spinosa; the plant Plumbago Zeylanica; the seed of Trigonella Fœnum Græcum; N. of a Nāga; N. of a man; (आ), f., N. of a plant, = ज्योतिष्मती; (अम्), n., N. of a luminous weapon with which Arjuna destroyed Tamas or darkness personified (see Mahā-bh. Droṇa-parva 1325); N. of the shining peak of the Meru.
ज्योतिस्: ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. light in various forms and under various aspects, as the light of the sun, of dawn, of fire, of lightning, &c.; brightness or clearness of the sky, daylight (opposed to Tamas); lightning; light ap-pearing in three forms, viz. fire on the earth, ether or air in the intermediate region, and sun in the sky; a glance of the eye, the faculty of seeing, the eye; the heavenly bodies, the planets and stars (in this sense pl., e. g. ज्योतिषाम् अयनम्, the course of the heavenly bodies); sun and moon (in this sense du., e. g. ज्योतिषोर् उपसर्गाः, eclipses &c. of the sun and moon); the light of heaven, the celestial world; light as the divine principle of life or as the source of intelligence, intelligence; light as a type of freedom, of bliss and of victory, [cf. Lat. lux and Gr. φάος, φῶς]; N. of the Jyotiṣṭoma as applied to the first and sixth days of the Abhi-plava ceremony which lasts six days; N. of certain formularies containing the word ज्योतिस्; a kind of metre consisting of thirty-two short and sixteen long syllables; the science of the course of the heavenly bodies, &c., see ज्योतिष; a mystical term for the letter र्; (इस्), m. fire; the sun; N. of the plant Trigonella Fœnum Græcum; N. of a son of Manu Svārociṣa; also of Marut; [cf. चित्र-ज्योतिस् and दक्षिणा-ज्°।] —ज्योतिः-शास्त्र, अम्, n. the science of astronomy; a work upon astronomy. —ज्योतिः-सामन्, अ, n., N. of a Sāman. —ज्योतिः-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m. title of an astronomical work. —ज्योतिर्-अग्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. preceded by light or life. —ज्योतिरथ्या, f., N. of a river; (a wrong form for ज्योती-रथा।) —ज्योतिर्-अनीक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a shining face or appearance. —ज्योतिर्-इङ्ग or ज्योतिर्-इङ्गण, अस्, m. ‘moving light,’ a fire-fly. —ज्योतिर्-ईश or ज्योतिर्-ईश्वर, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Dhūrta-samāgama. —ज्योतिर्-गण, अस्, m. the heavenly bodies collectively. —ज्योतिर्-जरायु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. surrounded by a brilliant covering; (Sāy.) brilliant (among the clouds) like an embryo. —ज्योतिर्-ज्ञ, अस्, m. ‘star-knower,’ an astrologer, one versed in astronomy. —ज्योतिर्-ज्वलनार्चि-श्री-गर्भ (°न-अर्°), अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva. —ज्योतिर्-धामन्, आ, m., N. of one of the seven sages in the Manv-antara of Tāmasa. —ज्योतिर्-भास-मणि, इस्, m. a kind of gem. —ज्योतिर्-भासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, brilliant with light. —ज्योतिर्-मण्डल, अम्, n. the stellar sphere. —ज्योतिर्-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, con-sisting of light, brilliant, abounding with stars, starry. —ज्योतिर्मिलिन्, ई, m. (for -मालिन् ?), a fire-fly. —ज्योतिर्-मुख, अस्, m., N. of one of the monkey-followers of Rāma. —ज्योतिर्-लिङ्ग, अम्, n., N. of several Liṅga temples. —ज्योतिर्-लेखावलयिन्, ई, इनी, इ, studded with rows of stars. —ज्योतिर्-लोक, अस्, m. the world of light. —ज्योतिर्-विद्, त्, त्, त्, knowing the stars, an astronomer; creating light (in this sense rt. 3. विद्, to find). —ज्योतिर्-विद्या, f. the science of astronomy, astrology. —ज्योतिर्-वीज, अम्, n. ‘seed of light,’ a fire-fly. —ज्योतिर्-हस्ता, f. an epithet of Durgā. —ज्योतिश्-चक्र, अम्, n. ‘circle of the luminaries,’ the zodiac. —ज्योतिष्-कण, अस्, m. a spark of fire. —ज्योतिष्-कर, अस्, m. ‘light-causer,’ a kind of flower. —ज्योतिष्-कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, like flame or fire, blazing, radiant. —ज्योतिष्कल्प-लता, f. title of an astrological work. —ज्योतिष्-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make light, illumine. —ज्योतिष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. creating light. —ज्योतिष्-टम, अस्, आ, अम्, diffusing the most brilliant light. —ज्योतिष्टोम, अस्, m. (fr. ज्योतिस्-स्तोम), a Soma ceremony considered as the typical form of a whole class of ceremonies; it consists of either four or seven subdivisions, viz. the Agni-ṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍa-śin, Ati-rātra, or in addition to these the Atyagni-ṣṭoma, Vāja-peya, and Aptor-yāma. —ज्योतिष्-ट्व, अम्, n. luminousness, illumination; the condition of light. —ज्योतिष्-पक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, having brilliant wings. —ज्योतिष्-प्रभ, अस्, m. ‘brilliant with light,’ N. of a kind of flower; N. of a Buddha; also of a Bodhi-sattva. —ज्योतिष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, luminous, brilliant, shining, belonging to the world of light, heavenly, celestial; ज्योतिष्मती त्रिष्टुप्, a form of the Triṣṭubh metre, containing three Pādas of twelve syllables each and one Pāda of eight syllables; (आन्), m. the sun; N. of one of the seven suns appearing at the destruction of the world; N. of the third foot of Brahmā; N. of a son of Manu Svāyambhuva; also of Manu Sāvarṇa; N. of a king of Kuśa-dvīpa; also of a son of Priya-vrata; N. of a mountain; (ती), f. the night (as illumined by the stars), heart-pea, Cardiospermum Halicacabum. —ज्योतिस्-सात्, ind. to flame, to fire or light; ज्योतिस्सात् कृ, to light, illumine, set on fire. —ज्योती-रत, अस्, m., N. of a serpent-demon. —ज्योती-रथ, अस्, आ, अम्, whose chariot is light; (Sāy.) bearing fire or the oblation like a chariot; (अस्), m. the pole-star or in mythology Dhruva, son of Uttāna-pāda; a kind of serpent; (आ), f., N. of a river which joins the Śoṇa or Sone. —ज्योती-रस, अस्, m. a kind of gem. —ज्योती-रूप-स्वयम्भू, ऊस्, m. Svayambhū (Brahmā) in the form of light. —ज्योती-रूपेश्वर (°प-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga.
ज्योत्स्ना: ज्योत्स्ना, f. a moonlight night; moonlight; light, splendor in general; N. of one of the bodies of Brahmā; N. of one of the sixteen Kalās of the moon; an epithet of Durgā; N. of two plants, = ज्योत्स्नी and घोषातकी. —ज्योत्स्ना-काली, f., N. of a daughter of the moon and wife of Puṣkara who was a son of Varuṇa. —ज्योत्स्ना-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘a friend of the moonlight,’ the bird Chakora or Greek partridge. —ज्योत्स्ना-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, illuminated by the moon, shining, brilliant. —ज्योत्स्ना-वृक्ष, अस्, m. the tree or tripod of a lamp, a lamp-stand, candlestick. —ज्योत्स्नेश (°ना-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord or husband of the moonlight,’ the moon.
ज्योत्स्निका: ज्योत्स्निका, f., N. of a plant, = कोषातकी।
ज्योत्स्नी: ज्योत्स्नी, f. a moonlight night; a small cucumber, Trichosanthes Diœca; a kind of perfume, = रेणुका; (a wrong form for ज्यौत्स्नी।)
ज्यौतिष: ज्यौतिष, अम्, n., N. of a Sāman.
ज्यौतिषिक: ज्यौतिषिक, अस्, m. one who knows the Jyotiṣa, an astronomer, astrologer.
ज्यौत्स्न: ज्यौत्स्न, अस्, ई, अम्, luminous especially with moonlight; (अस्), m. the time of moonlight, the light half of a month; (ई), f. a full moon night; N. of a plant, = पटोलिका।
ज्यौत्स्निका: ज्यौत्स्निका, f. a moonlight night; (perhaps an incorrect form for ज्योत्स्निका।)
ज्यो: ज्यो ज्यो, cl. 1. A. ज्यवते, &c., to advise, instruct, order; observe a vow or any reli-gious obligation.
ज्योक्: ज्योक् ज्योक्, ind. long, for a long time, for a long while; ज्योक्तमाम्, superl. ind. for the longest time, longest. —ज्योग्-जीवातु, उस्, f. long life; ज्योक् कृ, to be long about anything, delay.
ज्योडि: ज्योडि ज्योडि, in names of plants. Cf. कर-ज्योडि and हस्त-ज्°।
ज्योतयमानक: ज्योतयमानक ज्योतयमानक, अस्, इका, अम्, Ved. shining (?).
ज्योतिक: ज्योतिक ज्योतिक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; (perhaps a wrong reading for ज्योतिष्क।)
ज्यौ: ज्यौ ज्यौ, औस्, m. (a word borrowed fr. the Gr. Ζεύς), the planet Jupiter.
ज्रि: ज्रि 1. ज्रि, cl. 1. P. ज्रयति, &c., to over-power, conquer; to go.
2. ज्रि, इस्, इस्, इ, in उरु-ज्रि, q. v.
ज्रि 3. ज्रि or ज्री [cf. rt. 1. जॄ], cl. 1. 10. 9. P. ज्रयति, ज्राययति, ज्रिणाति, &c., to grow old, to be or become old or decayed.
ज्रयस्: ज्रयस्, अस्, n., Ved. a plain, expanse, space; (Sāy.) speed; splendor; overpowering; [cf. Zend zarajo.]
ज्रयसान: ज्रयसान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. spreading, expanding, occupying space; (Sāy.) going.
ज्वर्: ज्वर् ज्वर्, cl. 1. P. ज्वरति, जज्वार, ज्वरि-ष्यति, अज्वारीत्, ज्वरितुम्, to be feverish, to be hot with fever or passion, to be diseased &c.: Caus. P. ज्वरयति, -यितुम्, to make feverish: Desid. जिज्वरिषति: Intens. जाज्वर्यते, जाजूर्ति; [cf. Lat. a-ger; Hib. gurt, ‘pain, trouble, fierceness;’ Germ. schwer; Old Germ. swâr, swâri; Germ. quâlen ?].
ज्वर्; add — connected with rt. ज्वल्।
ज्वर: ज्वर, अस्, m. fever of different kinds (called after the different doṣas or humors of the body which are supposed to be affected by them; fever is called the leader and king of all diseases); fever of the soul, mental pain, affliction, grief, trouble, sorrow, distress; (आ), f. fever; (अस्, आ, अम्), heated, raging (with fever, passion, &c.), excited, inflamed. —ज्वर-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, febrifuge, anti-febrile, dispelling fever or ague; (अस्), m. or according to some (ई), f. the plant Cocculus Cordifolius, = गुडूची; the plant Chenopodium Album, = वास्तूक. —ज्वर-चिकित्सा, f. medical treatment of fever. —ज्वर-नाशक, अस्, आ, अम्, febrifuge. —ज्वर-निर्णय, अस्, m., N. of a medical work. —ज्वर-प्रतीकार, अस्, m. cure of fever. —ज्वर-हन्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, febrifuge; (त्री), f. the plant Rubia Munjista. —ज्वराग्नि (°र-अग्°), इस्, m. feverish heat, the hot paroxysm in fever. —ज्वराङ्कुश (°र-अङ्°), अस्, m. a febrifuge; the plant Andropogon Jvarancusa; title of a work on medicine. —ज्वराङ्गी (°र-अङ्°), f., N. of a plant, = भद्र-दन्तिका. —ज्वरान्तक (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, febrifuge, dispelling fever; (अस्), m. the plant Cathartocarpus Fistula; a kind of Nimba growing in Nepal. —ज्वरान्वित (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, suffering from fever or ague. —ज्वरापह (°र-अप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, febrifuge; (आ), f. a febrifuge, the plant Medicago Esculenta, = विल्ल-पत्त्री (?).
ज्वरित: ज्वरित, अस्, आ, अम्, or ज्वरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, febrile, feverish, affected with fever.
ज्वल्: ज्वल् ज्वल्, cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) ज्वलति, -ते, जज्वाल, ज्वलिष्यति, अज्वालीत्, ज्वलि-तुम्, to burn brightly, blaze, flame, glow, shine; to burn (as a wound); to be ardent: Caus. P. ज्वाल-यति and ज्वलयति, -यितुम्, to set on fire, light, kindle, make radiant, illuminate: Desid. जिज्वलि-षति: Intens. जाज्वल्यते, जाज्वल्ति, to flame vio-lently, shine strongly, be brilliant; [cf. Hib. gual-laim, ‘I blacken, burn;’ gual, ‘coal, coals, fire:’ Germ. Kohle: Old Germ. colo: Eng. coal: Lith. swelù: Old Germ. wallu, walm, wâli.]
ज्वल: ज्वल, अस्, आ, अम्, flaming, blazing, shining, bril-liant; (अस्), m. flame, blaze, light. —ज्वल-मुखी, f., N. of a tutelary deity in the family of Lomaśa; [cf. ज्वाला-मुखी।] —ज्वलानन (°ल-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the face flaming. —ज्वला-रासभका-मय, अस्, m. = जाल-गर्दभ।
ज्वलका: ज्वलका, f. a large flame or blaze.
ज्वलत्: ज्वलत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, burning, blazing; shining, radiant, brilliant. —ज्वलन्-मणि, इस्, इस्, इ, blazing with jewels; (इस्), m. a brilliant gem.
ज्वलन: ज्वलन, अस्, आ, अम्, inflammable, combustible, flaming, shining; (अस्), m. fire; a N. of the numeral 3; corrosive alkali; the plant Plumbago Zeylanica; (आ), f., N. of a daughter of Takṣaka and wife of Ṛceyu [cf. ज्वाला]; (अम्), n. burning, blazing. —ज्वलनाश्मन् (°न-अश्°), आ, m. the sun-stone; [cf. सूर्य-कान्त।]
ज्वलनीय: ज्वलनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be burnt, combustible.
ज्वलयत्: ज्वलयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, kindling, burning, illu-mining, blazing, radiant.
ज्वलित: ज्वलित, अस्, आ, अम्, kindled, burnt, blazing, flam-ing; (तृणेषु ज्वलितं त्वया, you have lighted a fire in the grass, i. e. you have had easy work.) —ज्वलित-नयन, अस्, आ, अम्, fiery-eyed, looking angrily or fiercely; also ज्वलित-चक्षुस्, ज्वलित-नेत्र, &c. —ज्वलितानन (°त-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the face flaming.
ज्वलिन्: ज्वलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, burning, flaming, shining; (इनी), f. the plant Sanseviera Zeylanica, = मूर्वा।
ज्वाल: ज्वाल, अस्, ई, अम्, burning, blazing; (अस्), m. light, flame, a torch; (आ), f. a blaze, flame, illumination; burnt rice; N. of a daughter of Takṣaka and wife of Ṛkṣa; [cf. Hib. gual, ‘coal.’] —ज्वाला-खर-गद and ज्वाला-गर्दभक, अस्, m. = जाल-गर्द-भ. —ज्वालाग्नि (°ल-अग्°), इस्, m. blazing fire, flame. —ज्वाला-जिह्व, अस्, m. ‘flame-tongued,’ N. of fire; N. of an attendant of Skanda; of Śiva; of a Dānava. —ज्वाला-ध्वज, अस्, m. ‘flame-marked,’ fire. —ज्वा-ला-मुख, अस्, m. ‘flame-mouthed,’ a class of demons; (ई), f. a volcano; any place where subterranean fire or inflammable gas breaks forth, such places being held sacred by the Hindūs as indicating the presence of a form of Durgā; (a celebrated Jvālā-mukhī exists in the hills north-east of the Pañjāb to which pilgrim-ages are made; the soil abounds with carburetted hydrogen gas which takes fire upon coming in con-tact with the external air. According to the legend, the flame proceeds from the fire which the wife of Śiva created and in which she burned herself. Śiva finding that this flame was about to consume the world, buried it in the hollow of the mountain. According to another legend, the tongue of Pārvatī fell at this place. There is a similar volcanic region in Chinese Tartary where fire is produced by digging into the earth.) —ज्वाला-लिङ्ग, अम्, n. ‘flame-liṅga,’ N. of a temple of Śiva. —ज्वाला-वक्त्र, अस्, m. ‘flame-mouthed,’ N. of an attendant of Śiva. —ज्वालेश्वर (°ल-ईश्°), N. of a Tīrtha.
ज्वालिन्: ज्वालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, flaming, blazing; (इनी), f. mystical name of the letter व्।
जङ्घन्यमान: जङ्घन्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens.), being repeatedly struck, being greatly wounded.
जुह्वान: जुह्वान, अस्, आ, अम्, sacrificing, offering, present-ing; accepting (an offering, Ved.).
जडय: जडय, Nom. P. जडयति, &c., to make apa-thetic, make motionless or lifeless.
जडात्मक: जडात्मक, अस्, आ, अम्, or जडात्मन् (°ड-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, insensible, void of sensation, calm, placid, cool (said of the moon).
जाती: जाती, f. a kind of jasmine.
